function: Over-the-air gradient aggregation for semi-federated learning: power scaling, normalizing factors and receive beamformers chosen to amplify distortion and speed convergence while minimizing energy (p. 4, 8-11).
system: Uplink AirComp: BS with 16 antennas, 20 single-antenna devices in a 100 m x 100 m urban square, single-carrier waveforms, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3-4, 11).
method: Federated plus split learning (SemiFL) with AirComp gradient aggregation, training MLP, CNN and ResNet; resource allocation by closed-form, DC programming and CVX solvers, not learned (p. 2-11).
data_channel: CDL channel model of 3GPP TR 38.901 (ref. [43]) in a 100 m x 100 m urban square; Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 for the learned model (p. 11, 23).
test_conditions: Learning curves per setting: IID and non-IID data, several epsilon-1 values, and in the appendix imperfect Rayleigh or Rician CSI and alpha-stable noise; no cross-condition test (p. 12-16).
baselines: Earlier OTA FL designs: alpha-stable FL [29], MMSE&CI FL [49],[50]; energy baselines: SDR beamformer, max transmit power, max CPU, random data allocation; own ablations and SemiFedAvg (p. 12-14).
metrics: Classification accuracy and training loss versus rounds; overall uploading and computing energy consumption, also versus the maximum latency per round (p. 12-15, 17).
complexity: Order of complexity of Algorithm 2: O((K+2)N2 + (K+1)Nr^4.5 N1 N2 + (K+1)N2 + (K+1)^3 N2); Algorithm 3 has the same form with N3 (p. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 11: "We adopt a clustered delay line multiple-input multiple-output link-level fading channel model to generate the channel coefficient vectors for gradient aggregation" and data uploading, citing [43]; p. 23: "document TR 38.901, V16.1.0, 3GPP" is reference [43].
q2_support: p. 16: "To examine the robustness of the proposed approach under both imperfect CSI" - Fig. 14 gives one learning curve per channel or noise setting; no model trained under one condition is tested on another, so this is a CSI and noise sweep.
q3_support: p. 12: "FL with MMSE and CI (MMSE&CI FL) [49], [50]" is an earlier published aggregation design and "SemiFL with proposed algorithms outperforms the widely adopted MMSE&CI FL scheme in all cases"; p. 14: "SDR Beamformer [41]" is a non-learned baseline compared on energy.
q4_support: p. 10: "The main complexity of Algorithm 2 is given by" an order expression in K, Nr, N1 and N2; p. 11: "the complexity of Algorithm 3 can be given by" the same form.
q5_support: p. 12: "we train a MLP, a CNN, and a ResNet to classify the Fashion-MNIST [44], CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100" - public datasets of the learning task alone; the channels are simulated (p. 11) and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included as area 7: the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation of gradients (AirComp power scaling, normalizing factors, receive beamformers); the resource-allocation algorithms are closed-form, DC programming and CVX (not learned), and the learned element is the model trained with SemiFL. The CPU frequency and the data split between devices and BS sit above the physical layer but are optimized jointly with the aggregation design, so the reviewer may confirm the area. q1 rests on the CDL model named on p. 11 and on reference [43] being 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 23); the body text never writes 3GPP. q3 counts alpha-stable FL [29] and MMSE&CI FL [49],[50] as earlier aggregation designs and SDR, max power and random allocation as non-learned baselines; the ablations (Algo. 2-only, Algo. 3-only, SemiFL-AE) and SemiFedAvg are variants and are not counted. The PDF includes the appendices (p. 15-22) that the main text cites as [36].
